title: Diagnose repeated worker processing failure and safe retry recovery
trigger: RabbitMQ has a live consumer but a customer ticket remains queued while the same request ID repeatedly produces worker job_failed events.
preconditions: capture request ID, queue state, worker logs, and dependency health before mitigation
confirm the affected message is a valid expected ticket.created event rather than a malformed or unsupported poison message
diagnostic_steps: check queue total, ready, unacknowledged, and consumer counts
correlate repeated worker job_started and job_failed logs for the same request ID
inspect worker error_type and error text for the failing processing operation
check API readiness, queue-health, PostgreSQL connectivity, Redis, and RabbitMQ broker health
check worker failure metrics and recent application/dependency changes
mitigation_steps: if evidence confirms a transient external processing condition and the corrective action is approved, clear only that condition
leave the healthy RabbitMQ consumer running so the durable message can retry naturally
do not restart RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, Redis, API, or worker solely to clear a processing exception
do not allow indefinite retry to substitute for escalation when the condition is permanent or unknown
validation_steps: the same request ID produces a job_completed event after earlier job_failed events
queue total, ready, and unacknowledged counts return to zero
consumer count remains at the expected value
worker and API runtime identities remain unchanged
customer ticket read and core dependency health remain successful
escalation_boundary: Escalate to application/L3 or the owning dependency team if the processing exception cannot be safely corrected, if retries continue after the expected recovery, if the message is permanently malformed/unsupported, or if a source/configuration change is required. A permanently failing message belongs to the poison-message/quarantine path rather than unlimited requeue.
